start.text: Hild rows the way she talks: plainly, and without hurry. Kindleby's candles go small astern, a row of sparks along the wall, then a smudge, then gone.
Ring's north of us now. You'll not see it again till we're back. Keep your eyes on the ember and your ears to yourself.
Then the singing. Not ahead of you: around you. Voices, a great many, near enough to be in the boat with you, none of them saying anything you can catch.
...That's it. Evening office, and the door shut. Louder than I remember. Louder.

She doesn't stop rowing. Black rocks go by close enough to touch, streaming, and she threads them without looking round. Ahead, on the biggest of them, a squat dark tower; and under it one small light, a lamp held out low by someone standing very still.
He's alive, then. Iver Lusk. ...He'll have been listening to that for three months.
I'll bide with the boat. Go on up. Mind the cairns: the old brothers stood one wherever the bottom will bear you, and nowhere else.
